articles.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.description: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
key_points: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.
Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.

articles.title: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
articles.description: Experts warn that using AI to enhance property images can go too far and mislead prospective buyers.
articles.summary: The images Olivia Nicole saw of a home on Rightmove (l) were completely different to how the property looked in real life (r) Have you ever been impressed by the pictures of a property on an estate agent's website, only to find the place looks completely different when you view…
key_points: Then there's a chance that AI was used to enhance the images you saw.
From repainted walls to imaginary lawns, estate agents are increasingly using the technology to make homes seem more appealing, arguing it helps buyers visualise the potential of a place.
But experts warn it can go too far and mislead prospective buyers - a trend dubbed "housefishing".

articles.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
articles.description: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
articles.summary: Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.
key_points: Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported , external .
Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training…
He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

articles.description: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
